parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The file passes. CreateTaskUseCase.execute does normal application-layer work. It checks that the project exists through the ProjectRepository port, validates the incoming CreateTaskDto, builds the Task entity, assigns an id through the IdGenerator port and saves through the TaskRepository port. There's no persistence detail (no SQL or storage client), no transport or HTTP handling and no framework code.

The validation checks the shape of untrusted input: types, an empty title and an unparseable dueDate. Checking input at the use-case boundary is acceptable application work, and status parsing is left to the domain's parseTaskStatus. The borderline items are "title is required" and the default status "todo". These could be treated as Task invariants that belong in the domain entity. Even so, they don't put a responsibility from another layer kind (persistence, transport or presentation) into this file. No ADR prose was given to contradict this.
